derived.hit_copy_diagnosis: 474 slabs x 3 cudaMemcpy = 1422 calls at ~62-65us/call -> call-overhead dominated, not bandwidth (4.4 GB at only 47 GB/s)

derived.decode_ceiling_faithful: ~6-8 t/s with every loader cost removed (kernels + attention/dense remain); consistent with research doc's 5.5-9. Only levers past it: fewer bytes/token (MTP drafting multiplier) or faster kernel read path

ranked_next_levers_by_measured_value: 1. async/batched hit copies + fills (92.5+34.5 -> ~20 ms; ~30 lines, no kernel changes) then re-measure before deciding on full zero-copy pointer-indirection
2. arena 68 -> ~86 GB in GLM-only serving (DSV4 not resident): LRU curve puts hit ~85%, fetch 215 -> ~130 ms — pure config
3. GGUF slab repack (gate|up|down contiguous per expert): fetch granularity 3.1 -> 9.3 MB, ~7.2 -> ~11-12.5 GB/s
4. GLM MTP block / drafting: multiplies effective t/s by accept length across the ENTIRE per-token cost — the only lever that beats the byte-arithmetic ceiling
5. kernel read-path bandwidth (55 GB/s effective vs ~200 attainable) — investigate before writing new kernels

mtp_probe_2026_07_25.identity_caveat: MTP output is NOT byte-identical to single-token decode: warm2/dec32 sha 6da984e6bb80 vs baseline 9113dfd0d233 (within-run stable: warm2==dec32). Cause: the 2-token verify batch takes the n_tokens>1 kernel path whose FP summation order differs, so greedy flips at near-ties. warm1 (first request, no draft state yet) matched baseline exactly. Any adoption requires the 100-case NLL fidelity suite re-run in MTP mode instead of byte-vs-baseline.
mtp_probe_2026_07_25.arena_bump_ruled_out: 86GB arena would breach the kill floor (engine non-arena RSS ~30 GiB; 97 total observed at 68GB arena). Safe max ~75GB buys only ~2-3 LRU hit points per the committed trace curve — not worth a window. The fetch levers are slab repack (read granularity 3.1->9.3MB) and admission policy (LRU 74% vs Belady 88% at same size).
